verdicts.reason: UserId names the users table; 79851 badges over 25078 users is badges-per-user, as in the Stack Exchange schema.
UserId names the users table; many comments per user, values are ordinary user ids.
UserId names the users table; the -1 sample is the Community user that users.Id also carries, which is what a real reference would contain.
LinkTypeId is a two-valued enum (1 linked, 3 duplicate) whose lookup table is not in this schema; tags is not a link type.
PostTypeId is a 7-valued enum (question, answer, wiki...) with no lookup table here; badges is not a post type.
OwnerUserId names the users table; 91966 posts over 21979 users is posts-per-author.
LastEditorUserId names the users table; a second role of user on posts, fewer distinct because most posts are never edited.
WikiPostId names a post; samples (20257, 62157, 67814) look like post ids, and each tag's wiki is a post -- 596 tags have one.
Age is an attribute with 70 distinct values that trivially fall inside a 303155-row surrogate sequence.
PostId names the posts table; many votes per post over 8584 posts.
VoteTypeId is a 10-valued enum (upvote, downvote, bounty...) with no lookup table here; posts is not a vote type.
UserId names the users table; only 509 distinct because votes record the user only for bounty types, which fits the schema, and the score is low only for that sparsity.
